verify.note: Closed 2026-09-29 (ADR-1656). Runs the real prebuild (scripts/snapshot-turbopack-cache.mjs) and postbuild gate (scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs) against a fixture cache whose Turbopack grows past the trim point after the snapshot: the gate must put the restored generation back, count the hold, and leave no snapshot to upload; with the count already at HOLD_LIMIT it must trim and reset. Fails on main at the first arm (prebuild takes no snapshot). Each arm mutation-fired: hold disabled, snapshot left behind, count not written, refresh removed.

append.detail: CLOSED 2026-09-29 (ADR-1656). PREMISE RE-TESTED (Vercel build logs of 2026-09-29, read only): it holds. node_modules 959 MiB on every build; a cold compile wrote 1293 MiB of Turbopack and uploaded 1.25 GB, the first warm build held 1459 MiB and uploaded 1.36 GB, and the trim fired three times in 22 production builds (dpl_4LyNMq4r, dpl_JCj4zdsa, dpl_4H4zhCnd, each uploading 264.71 MB), each followed by a cold compile. WHAT GROWS, reproduced on a small Next 16.3.6 Turbopack app over 22 warm builds: .next/cache/turbopack/<version> is one log-structured database; every warm build writes new .sst tables and .meta index files (about 12% of the cold size), the engine compacts only past its own duplication threshold (about every 7 builds), and the index files of small families are never merged, so the floor ratchets. RULED OUT, measured: pruning its files by age (every table is referenced by an index, so a deleted one is a database with a hole in it) and next internal post-build (turbopackDatabaseCompact reclaimed 0 bytes on a database 70% over its cold size). WHAT CLOSED IT: the growth is stopped at the upload instead of inside the engine. prebuild hard-links the restored cache into .next/cache/turbopack-restored (tables linked, CURRENT and LOG copied; md5 sums held across three warm builds including a compaction). When the cache a build wrote is over the trim point and the restored one fits and carries the same version directory, check:cache-budget puts the restored one back and the next build compiles warm (9.5 s against 79 s cold on the reproduction). HOLD_LIMIT = 6 holds in a row, counted in .next/cache/turbopack-held.json, then the trim runs as before and the next build compiles a fresh cache. The snapshot is weighed apart, never listed or trimmed, and removed before upload. Ceiling, reserve, PACKED_PER_RAW, the node_modules floor and the trim list are unchanged. TESTS: scripts/check-cache-budget-hold.test.ts runs both real files against fixture caches (hold, count, refresh at the limit, cold build, compiler upgrade, over-budget snapshot, snapshot not counted, link vs copy, abandoned snapshot) with two mutants. STILL TO READ after merge: consecutive production builds printing HELD or the green line with no cold compile between refreshes.
